papers.quote: Insulin resistance drops rapidly with the delivery of the placenta.

papers.population_and_size: Pregnancy with diabetes or GDM; no size.
papers.measure_type: Not applicable (guideline); mentions glucose-based tests only; insulin sensitivity physiology.

papers.relied_on: Empirical T2D figure +90%/-47% from 12 diet-controlled women; non-diabetic controls far less variable (MEAS-29).
papers.full_text_shows: Confirms design and numbers: fasting HOMA-IR measured at 4-day intervals on 10 consecutive occasions in 12 postmenopausal women with diet-controlled T2D and 11 matched controls. The +90%/-47% critical difference comes from 2.77 x CVI on log-transformed data and is given only for the T2D group. Control variation was Gaussian and smaller (mean intraindividual variation 1.05 vs 0.15, P<0.001; the unit is not clear in the extracted text).
papers.quote: a subsequent sample must increase by 90% or decrease by 47% to be considered significantly different from the first.
papers.key_numbers: HOMA-IR 4.33+-2.3 (T2D) vs 2.11+-0.79 (controls); +90%/-47%; insulin assay CV 10.6%; analytical variance 1.5% of total variance (T2D).
papers.role_in_work: Empirical anchor for the RCV discussion.
papers.population_and_size: 12 women T2D + 11 controls, postmenopausal, Caucasian; 10 occasions each, 4-day intervals.
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based HOMA-IR (fasting insulin, fasting glucose), 0800-0900 samples.
papers.assay_or_platform: DPC Immulite 2000 chemiluminescent insulin (CV 10.6%); Beckman Synchron LX20 glucose
papers.quality_note: Small, single-sex, single-ethnic group; no percent critical difference given for controls in the extracted text, so the 'far less variable' wording rests on the variation figures, not a control RCV.

papers.relied_on: Among-assay CV 12-66%, median 24%, for 10 assays; a common reference preparation did not lower it (MEAS-14, MEAS-12).
papers.full_text_shows: Abstract confirmed. Added detail: 12 assays from 9 manufacturers were evaluated but results are for 10; CV was measured on 40 patient samples and was greatest at low insulin concentrations; within-assay CV 3.7-39.0%; 6 of 10 assays met a 32% total-error limit; 7 of 10 recovered added insulin within 15.5%. Cross-reactivity with proinsulin varied.
papers.quote: A common insulin reference preparation did not change the among-assay CV and failed to improve harmonization of results among assays.
papers.key_numbers: among-assay CV 12-66%, median 24%; within-assay CV 3.7-39.0%; 40 patient samples; 6/10 within 32% total error.
papers.population_and_size: 12 commercial assays/9 manufacturers (10 analysed); 40 patient samples; serum pool.
papers.quality_note: Old-generation assays; CV depends on concentration, so the single median hides the range.

papers.relied_on: HOMA-IR ranges across 11 assays: 0.8-2.0 normoglycaemia, 1.9-3.2 prediabetes, 1.5-2.9 T2D (MEAS-10).
papers.full_text_shows: Text read; tables (Table 2, Fig. 1) are not in the extracted file, so the exact per-assay ranges 0.8-2.0, 1.9-3.2, 1.5-2.9 could not be checked. Text gives pooled medians (IQR): 1.30 (0.84-1.65) normoglycaemia, 2.58 (1.24-3.12) prediabetes, 2.13 (1.19-3.54) T2D, and 'HOMA estimates varied by up to twofold' by assay. Small groups (n=12, 18, 67; total 97). Calculator choice changed HOMA-IR by 15%; 4.3% of insulin results <20 pmol/L and 1% >300 pmol/L were out of calculator limits.
papers.quote: HOMA estimates varied by up to twofold, depending on which insulin assay was used.
papers.key_numbers: n=97 (12/18/67); up to twofold across 11 assays; calculator choice 15%; pooled median HOMA-IR 1.30/2.58/2.13.
papers.role_in_work: Source for assay dependence of HOMA-IR.
papers.design: Cross-sectional multi-assay comparison on one sample set.
papers.population_and_size: 97 fasting adults 18-75 y; 11 serum insulin assays plus one plasma assay; 5 runs.
papers.assay_or_platform: 11 insulin assays (mean QC CV 3.8% and above); IRP 66/304 calibrated.
papers.quality_note: Normoglycaemic group only 12; the figure ranges are likely from Table 2 (not in file); mark as not re-verified.

papers.relied_on: 8 assays, lowest and highest medians differ by factor 1.8; 'It reports no CV' (MEAS-15).
papers.full_text_shows: The factor 1.8 is confirmed (8.35 uIU/mL Diametra to 14.71 uIU/mL Roche). But the paper does report CVs: intra-assay CV 0.8-10.1% and inter-assay CV 1.0-12.9% from quality-control material. It does not report an among-assay CV. So 'reports no CV' is wrong as written.
papers.quote: serum insulin measurement with different assays showed a maximum of 1.8-fold difference
papers.key_numbers: 165 serum samples (85 fasting/80 non-fasting); 8 assays (2 CLIA, 4 ELISA, 2 IRMA); medians 8.35-14.71 uIU/mL; within-assay CVs 0.8-10.1%, inter-assay CVs 1.0-12.9%.
papers.design: Method-comparison study with Bland-Altman and Deming regression.
papers.population_and_size: 165 serum samples from 165 participants (65 men, 100 women); Iranian.
papers.assay_or_platform: Roche, DiaSorin, Tosoh, Mercodia, Monobind, Diametra, Izotop, BioSource
papers.quality_note: QC replicate design was below CLSI EP15-A2 (authors' own limitation); results not extrapolable to other assays.

papers.relied_on: Only one small study gives a HOMA-IR inter-laboratory figure (25%, ten samples, seven labs); DOI not recorded; Helsinki illustration not about one patient (MEAS-19, MEAS-48).
papers.full_text_shows: Confirms 25% (25.0%), ten non-diabetic individuals, seven laboratories; the 25% is driven by insulin (25.4%) not glucose (4.6%). HOMA-IR 2.0 in Helsinki corresponded to 1.3, 1.6, 1.8, 1.8, 2.0, 2.1 elsewhere, derived from regression of liver fat on HOMA-IR per centre (population-level, not one patient), so MEAS-48 holds. Lab means ranged 0.69-4.0 for HOMA-IR. The DOI is 10.1007/s00125-017-4340-1 (now recorded). Main population finding: upper 95th percentile HOMA-IR 1.9 and 2.0 (FINRISK n=1167, FIN-D2D n=459); NAFLD cut-off 1.9 (sensitivity 87%, specificity 79%).
papers.quote: The inter-laboratory CV% of HOMA-IR was 25% due to inter-assay variation in insulin (25%) rather than glucose (5%)
papers.key_numbers: inter-lab CV HOMA-IR 25.0%, insulin 25.4%, glucose 4.6%; lab mean HOMA-IR 0.69-4.0; NAFLD cut-off 1.9 (87%/79%); n=368 for NAFLD analysis.
papers.role_in_work: Single HOMA-IR inter-laboratory figure; also NAFLD HOMA-IR threshold.
papers.design: Population-based cohorts plus inter-laboratory sample exchange.
papers.population_and_size: FINRISK 1167, FIN-D2D 459, 368 non-diabetic with 1H-MRS; 10 individuals in 7 labs.
papers.assay_or_platform: Local assays in seven European labs (Helsinki Architect ci8200)
papers.quality_note: Ten samples, seven labs, non-diabetic persons only; storage at -80 C lowered insulin over time (sample handling).

papers.relied_on: DIETFITS n=609, prespecified diet x INS-30 interaction P=0.47, null; post-load insulin, weight-loss outcome (TRI-01, TRI-23, TRI-54).
papers.full_text_shows: Confirms n=609 and P=0.47 (3-way term, beta 0.08 per 10 uIU/mL, 95% CI -0.13 to 0.28). But the insulin hypothesis was added after the trial began (when funding rose) and before examining data; originally an insulin-sensitivity measure was planned. Power: more than 80% for the original n=400, about 90% post hoc for 609. The effect-modifier is the 30-minute insulin of a 75-g OGTT (proxy for insulin secretion), mean 93 uIU/mL. Adults 18-50, BMI 28-40, no diabetes.
papers.quote: Prior to examining any data, we modified the primary hypothesis of our study and tested baseline INS-30
papers.key_numbers: P=.47; beta 0.08 (-0.13 to 0.28) per 10 uIU/mL; n=609 (481 completed); weight change -5.3 kg (low fat) vs -6.0 kg (low carbohydrate).
papers.role_in_work: Randomized interaction test for post-load insulin as effect modifier of diet.
papers.design: Randomized clinical trial (12 months) with prespecified interaction tests.
papers.measure_type: Post-load (30-minute insulin after 75 g OGTT, INS-30), insulin not C-peptide.
papers.assay_or_platform: Insulin assay not named in main text.
papers.quality_note: Null result applies to non-diabetic overweight adults and weight loss only; 'prespecified' should read 'specified before data analysis, added after trial start'.

papers.relied_on: HOMA-IR, QUICKI and FIRI are monotone transforms of one another; QUICKI's 4.1% reflects its log transform and does not make it more informative (MEAS-08).
papers.full_text_shows: Confirms: one-to-one monotonic transforms, so Spearman, ROC and rank-based tests are identical; they are not linear transforms of each other (HOMA-IR and FIRI are linear, QUICKI is not). Simulation, not clinical data. The paper does not discuss within-person CV; the '4.1% reflects its log transform' remark is the project's inference.
papers.quote: We have shown that HOMA-IR, QUICKI and FIRI are one-to-one transformations of each other.
papers.key_numbers: HOMA-IR and QUICKI Spearman correlation -1; simulated Pearson with lean mass 0.75; advice to choose one of three.
papers.measure_type: Fasting surrogate indices (HOMA-IR, QUICKI, FIRI); OGTT indices discussed.
papers.quality_note: Equivalence is for rank-based methods only; parametric analyses can differ. Does not support the CV statement.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md line 47 (Tohidi 2017 bullet) and claims MEAS-15
claim_issues.issue: 'It reports no CV' is wrong; the paper reports intra-assay (0.8-10.1%) and inter-assay (1.0-12.9%) CVs from QC material. It reports no among-assay CV.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Tohidi 2017 (PMID 28150502, full text): 8 assays on 165 serum samples, lowest and highest median differing by a factor of 1.8; it reports within-assay CVs (intra-assay 0.8-10.1%, inter-assay 1.0-12.9%) but no among-assay CV.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md line 76 (DIETFITS table row) and TRI-01, TRI-23

claim_issues.proposed_wording: DIETFITS (PMID 29466592, full text): n=609; diet x 30-minute post-glucose insulin interaction, specified before data were examined but added after the trial began, P = 0.47 (beta 0.08 per 10 uIU/mL, 95% CI -0.13 to 0.28); non-diabetic adults, weight loss outcome.

claim_issues.issue: Local full text is the executive summary only; Table 2 and 'risk factor and mechanism' wording not verifiable here. Keep the excerpt label.
